document_notes: Page 222 contains the entry for L. Arruntius, consul in 6 AD, who was appointed legatus Augusti pro praetore of Hispania Citerior but governed in absence.

entries.relevance_notes: Explicitly identified as 'legatus Augusti pro praetore' of Hispania (citeriorem), though he governed the province in absence (absens gubernare coactus est).

Seiani) ἡρημένον μὲν πρὸ δέκα ἐτῶν ᾿Ιβηρίας ἄρξαι (v. supra), κρινόμενον δὲ ἐπί τισιν ἐξ ἐκείνου ἀφῆκε, καὶ δ αὐτὸν καὶ τοῖς ἄλλοις τοῖς ἡγεμονεύσειν τινῶν ἢ καὶ ἀλλο τι δημόσιον πράξειν μέλλουσιν ἄδειαν ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τούτῳ τῶν τοιούτων δικῶν ἔδωκε. Philol. 26, 1931, 37 sq., qui simul monuit ad eandem rem pertinere quae traduntur dig. 48, 2, 12 hos accusare non licet: legatum imperatoris ex sententia Lentuli dicta Sulla et Trione consulibus (qui fasces tenuerunt a kal. Iuliis usque ad kal. Octobres a. 31). governorship_factoids.exact_text: Hispaniam (citeriorem) regendam accepit (legatus Augusti pro praetore), sed provinciam absens gubernare coactus est, a Tiberio ob metum Romae retentus
notes: Arruntius was appointed to govern Hispania Citerior but was forced to govern in absence because Tiberius detained him in Rome out of fear.

Tacitus (Ann. 6, 27) states in 33 AD that Arruntius had been detained for ten years, though L. Piso was in charge of Hispania Citerior in 25 AD. It is probable that Arruntius succeeded Piso after the latter's death in 25 AD.
